assertion.statement: Prime-to-q ideal quotients correspond to the same adelic lattice multiplication, with one uniform inverse ideal convention.
assertion.objects: Enhanced prime-to-q Tate lattices, covariant q-Dieudonne convention, right Hom module, CM ideal a prime to Nq.
assertion.hypotheses: The quotient and its endomorphisms exist by retained good-reduction facts; source geometric/Tate classification and O action are fixed.
assertion.quantifiers: Every prime-to-Nq ideal representative and every prime component of the fixed reference realization.
assertion.parameter_range: q=ell_0 odd prime; all positive N coprime to q, with arbitrary prime-power exponents including2; choose auxiliary p outside Nq.
assertion.uniformity: Exact geometric classification and actions; no asymptotic bound or discriminant size condition.
assertion.constants: No class-number or automorphism quotient factor is inserted; Frobenius has order dividing2 on the coarse set.
assertion.normalizations: At l!=q use usual Tate modules; at q use Ribet transpose of contravariant Dieudonne module. Quotient replaces Lambda_l by a_l^-1 Lambda_l, hence z by a^-1 z.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not use an etale rank-two q-adic Tate module; do not conflate a transporter with its inverse. No source claim supplies quotient-specialization existence.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the ideal quotient using retained inputs, then compare its lattices in the same rational identification.

assertion.exceptional_cases: No effective selected prime-size bound or nonvanishing theorem is claimed.
assertion.limit_order: Fix q,a and the finite forbidden set; let x grow past both fixed thresholds; theta>x/(2phi(q)) is unbounded.

original_use.reason: The Weil pairing identifies the finite module with its Tate dual. The actual rational two-torsion gives integral plus/minus eigenlattices as stated in the caller. Its explicit rectangular-lattice Kummer computation gives the minus line of order2. H1 has the two order2 summands from these eigenlattices. Pairing two cocycles valued in the same minus eigenline gives zero by the alternating Weil pairing. The line is therefore isotropic and has half the dimension of this nondegenerate two-dimensional F2 space, hence is its own annihilator.

The already established equality at that prime gives equality on the chosen element. This proves character equality without using the conditional Euler formula or semisimple representation theory.

available_assertion.statement: For a finite abelian extension of number fields, every element of its Galois group occurs as Frobenius at unramified primes outside any fixed finite excluded set.
available_assertion.objects: A finite abelian extension and its finite Galois group.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The extension is finite and abelian; exclude ramified primes and an arbitrary fixed finite set.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every group element and every such finite exclusion set.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Finite abelian extensions only.
available_assertion.uniformity: Existence outside each fixed finite set; no effective bound on the prime is asserted.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical prime bound is supplied.
available_assertion.normalizations: Arithmetic Frobenius; inversion of the convention preserves the resulting character-equality implication.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No semisimple trace determination or rational compatible-system theorem is imported.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix the finite extension, element and finite exclusions before choosing the prime.

needed_assertion.statement: The two induced Dirichlet characters in C4 are equal if their values agree at every common good prime.
needed_assertion.objects: The two finite-order Dirichlet characters compared in the coefficient-conjugate newform argument at anchor line31.
needed_assertion.hypotheses: Both characters factor through a common finite abelian quotient; their values at every prime outside the finite bad set agree, as supplied by the displayed coefficient formula.
needed_assertion.quantifiers: For the two actual characters and all elements of their common finite quotient.
needed_assertion.parameter_range: The fixed levels and character moduli in C4; primes outside their finite bad set.
needed_assertion.uniformity: Only equality for this pair; no field, level or coefficient enlargement is inferred.
needed_assertion.constants: No effective prime bound or quantitative estimate.
needed_assertion.normalizations: Character value at a good prime equals its value on arithmetic Frobenius.
needed_assertion.exceptional_cases: The coefficient identity and same-form/primitive-source hypotheses are retained inputs. The Euler-factor formula and semisimple trace lemma are not premises.
needed_assertion.limit_order: Fix the common finite abelian quotient; apply density outside the bad set; deduce equality on every quotient element.
